number.why: The published omarigliptin-versus-placebo HR for first 3-point MACE is exactly 1.00 (95% CI 0.77–1.29). The ruling correctly flags that the source-defined ITT population excludes randomized participants who received no medication. However, the served timepoint needs qualification: the estimate covers the final analysis cutoff, not every patient's final study visit.

quotes.span: The primary MACE outcome occurred in 114/2092 patients in the omarigliptin group (5.45%; 2.96/100 patient-years) and 114/2100 patients in the placebo group (5.43%; 2.97/100 patient-years), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77, 1.29).
time to first major adverse CV event (MACE, the composite of CV death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke)

The population analyzed was the ITT population that included all randomized patients who took at least 1 dose of blinded study medication and all CV endpoint data, regardless of the time since a patient may have discontinued blinded study medication.
The analyses presented herein encompass the time period from first-patient-first-visit (October 16, 2012) to the final data cut-off date (May 13, 2016).

CV events that occurred after the data cut-off date in the remaining 9.6% of patients (n = 403; 209 in the omarigliptin group and 194 in the placebo group) who were ongoing in the study at the time of the data cut-off date were not adjudicated and are not included in the analyses presented herein.

entry.why: Eligibility establishes adults with T2DM. Requiring established cardiovascular disease narrows the enrolled population within the question's population. The intervention and randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled comparison also match.

quotes.span: Eligible patients were at least 40 years old with a history of T2DM and established CV disease.
Omarigliptin is a once-weekly (q.w.) oral DPP-4 inhibitor

In this randomized, double-blind study, 4202 patients with T2DM and established CV disease were assigned to either omarigliptin 25 mg q.w. or matching placebo in addition to their existing diabetes therapy.

missed: The ruling did not distinguish the May 13, 2016 analysis cutoff from complete study-end follow-up; the number quotes document excluded later events. This requires qualifying the served 'trial end' label, without changing the numerical estimate or entry ruling. The served unqualified 'intention-to-treat' label should also retain the dose-restricted definition already recognized by the ruling.
